includedPullRequests.title: Watch: stop 0 U boluses after a reconnect, time out Processing, expire entries after 2 min
includedPullRequests.body:
## Problem

A bolus entered on the Apple Watch can be sent to the phone as **0 U**, and the watch then stays on "Processing…" indefinitely.

Seen in practice: a user dialed 3 U, reached the confirm screen, lowered and raised their wrist, then turned the crown to confirm. The watch log shows `Bolus of 0 U requested`; the phone log shows `Watch requested bolus of 0.0 U` and nothing after it. No insulin was delivered and the watch never left "Processing…".

Three bugs combine:

1. **A reconnect clears the entry being confirmed.** `WatchState.sessionReachabilityDidChange` reset `bolusAmount`, `carbsAmount` and `confirmationProgress` every time the phone became reachable again, which happens on each wrist raise. The confirm screen is bound to those same values, so the amount became 0 while it was on screen.
2. **Nothing refuses a 0 U bolus, and the phone doesn't answer one.** The watch sent it, and `APSManager.enactBolus` returned early for `amount <= 0` without calling its callback, so the watch got no acknowledgment.
3. **"Processing…" never times out.** `AcknowledgementPendingView` started its 5 s fallback in `onChange(of: showCommsAnimation)`, but the flag is already `true` when the view appears, so the fallback never ran. The `sendMessage` error handlers only logged.

## Changes

Watch:
- Reachability changes no longer touch entries in progress. The main view still resets them when it appears.
- `sendBolusRequest` refuses amounts of 0 or less with a visible message.
- Every treatment request (bolus, carbs, override, temp target) shows "iPhone not reachable. Nothing was sent." instead of an empty screen when the phone is unreachable.
- `WatchState` times out a missing answer after 15 s, and ends the wait on a send error, with "No answer from iPhone. Check Trio on your iPhone before trying again." A send error does not prove the request wasn't delivered: in the logs from this report, a message reported as failed (not reachable) was delivered about 2 s later. So the message points the user to the phone instead of saying the request failed. The view-level timer is removed.
- **Entries expire 2 minutes after their last edit.** Confirming with the crown, or "Log Carbs", sends only an entry edited in the last 2 minutes; an older one is cleared and the watch says nothing was sent. When the app becomes active again, an entry older than 2 minutes is cleared and the watch returns to the main screen. Returning to the main screen, Cancel and sending end the entry. This replaces the reset-on-reconnect, which was presumably there to avoid stale amounts.

Phone:
- `enactBolus` answers every caller with a failure ("Error! Bolus amount must be greater than 0 U.") for amounts of 0 or less, or amounts that round to 0 on the pump. This also covers quick-pick and remote bolus, which got no answer before.

## Tests

- **Watch** (`Trio Watch App Tests`): a reconnect keeps the bolus entry; 0 U and negative boluses are refused; unreachable requests say nothing was sent; the timeout fires, is cancelled by an answer, and a send error ends the wait; the 2 minute entry boundary; expired and unedited entries are not sent; fresh entries are sent; a stale entry is cleared when the app becomes active.
  - This target did not compile on `dev`: its tests used members that no longer exist (`isBolusCanceled`, `maxCOB`, the bolus cancel request) and `import SwiftUICore`, which Xcode 26 rejects. Those are removed or fixed here.
- **Phone** (`TrioTests/BolusSafetyTests/EnactBolusAmountTests.swift`): `enactBolus` with 0, -0.05, -3 and NaN calls back exactly once with a failure.

Not covered by automated tests: the view wiring (marking edits in the input views, the scene-phase check, popping to the main screen).

## Known, unchanged

- In the Meal & Bolus flow the watch sends carbs and bolus as two requests; the carbs answer ends the wait, so the bolus result isn't shown on the watch. Same as before this PR.
- The confirm screen shows the amount floored to the bolus increment but sends the unrounded value, which the phone rounds again.

includedPullRequests.title: fix(food-camera): Keep front-camera crops on the scan frame and avoid a mirroring exception
includedPullRequests.body:
Follow-up to #31. Front cameras that support sensor orientation compensation rotate a photo's pixels, so the scan-frame crop missed on them. Apple says every iPhone Duo front camera uses it. The camera now turns compensation off after setup and after every camera switch, as Apple recommends once you use the rotation coordinator. The photo connection also stops adjusting mirroring automatically before it sets mirroring, because the SDK header says setting it otherwise throws. The crop test now checks which way the result turned.

Tested: `FoodCameraCropTests` pass on the iOS 27.2 simulator. Not yet checked on a physical Duo.

Apple: [Build a great camera experience for iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111465/)

includedPullRequests.title: Remove localization strings for CFBundleName and CFBundleDisplayName
includedPullRequests.body: Fixes issue #1754 - stops the iPhone from using "Trio" as app name regardless of APP_DISPLAY_NAME in ConfigOverride.xcconfig OR display name in XCode being modified manually. Caused by the app name being defined as localized string, whilst the app name will never be translated. (in the official repo anyway)

includedPullRequests.title: Alert when Tidepool login is rejected
includedPullRequests.body:
When Tidepool rejects the stored login (e.g. after a password change), uploads fail silently and Settings still shows "Connected to Tidepool". TidepoolKit didn't clear the session on a rejected token refresh, so TidepoolService never raised its own "no longer authorized" alert, and Trio dropped plugin alerts anyway.

- Bump TidepoolKit to `0f127de` (tidepool-org/TidepoolKit#82), which drops the session on a 401 or 400 `invalid_grant` refresh, so the plugin's re-login alert fires
- Route TidepoolService `issueAlert`/`retractAlert` into `TrioAlertManager`; catalog entry in Device Alarms (Normal tier, "Services")
- Retract the re-login alert once logged in again, since TidepoolService doesn't
- Wire service delegates on first setup too, not only after relaunch
- Settings shows "Tidepool Login Required" with a red indicator when there is no session
- Home multi-use panel shows "Tidepool Login Required" (below dosing warnings, above What's New), tapping opens Tidepool settings
- Persist the login-required flag, since `TidepoolService` can't be restored without a session and the panel would otherwise vanish after a relaunch

Supersedes #1186. Closes #1183.
